test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 01 Dec, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following constitutions inspired for the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**USSR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of the USSR.
 
• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• These duties are listed in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• The Fundamental Duties serve as a reminder to Indian citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have certain duties to the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties emphasize the importance of a responsible citizenry in maintaining the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of the nation.
 
• Some of the duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem, and protecting the natural environment.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• This amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period by the Indira Gandhi government.
 
• In addition to the introduction of Fundamental Duties, it also brought significant changes to the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule, and the Union-State relations.
 
• This amendment aimed to give more power to the central government and reduce the autonomy of the states.
 
 
 
• **Part IV-A of the Constitution**
 
 
• This part was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• It contains Article 51A, which enumerates the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
 
• Part IV-A serves as a reminder that the citizens also have certain duties towards the nation, in addition to enjoying their rights.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A**
 
 
• This article lists the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India.
 
• It includes duties such as abiding by the Constitution, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.
 
• Although these duties are not enforceable by law, they are considered essential for the promotion of a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
